definition: Haphazard means done without plan or order.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word haphazard. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know haphazard should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Their haphazard road trip skipped maps altogether, chasing whichever exit sign promised pie or a view.
Offhand describes one unprepared moment — a remark tossed out — and stops well short of haphazard.
Unplanned stops short of haphazard: an unplanned picnic lacks a schedule, but the basket can still be packed neatly — haphazard means the order itself is gone.

Scattershot means aimed everywhere at once, hoping something hits — a scattershot job hunt blankets fifty companies with one resume. Haphazard is about missing order rather than wide aim: a haphazard search can stay in a single room and still follow no method at all.

Slapdash work is done fast and carelessly — the steps happen, but each one is rushed and sloppy. Haphazard goes after the plan itself: no order, no method, chance in charge. A slapdash painter skips the sanding; a haphazard one paints whichever wall is nearest.

Haphazard is more specific than 'messy' — a mess describes a state, while haphazard indicts the method: things done with no plan or order, left to chance at every step.

Castle Books has no sections.
Novels lean against tide tables; a cookbook from 1974 sits wedged between two atlases; the poetry, such as it is, migrates.
The owner insists the haphazard shelving is a philosophy, but regulars know better: books are simply shelved wherever a gap appears on the day they arrive.
Newcomers ask for a map and are handed a bookmark; a search that should take a minute can eat an afternoon.
Somehow the store survives, mostly on customers who came for one book and left with five they never meant to find.
